Subject: Logging & redaction controls - post-demo follow-up

Hi Aisha / Rajiv,

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap + proposed next steps on the logging/redaction items you asked about:

1) Recap of ask from today
- FintechCo needs clarity on what request/response fields we persist in logs (bodies, headers, trace IDs).
- PII redaction expectations (names, account numbers, emails, SSN-like identifiers).
- Retention window requirements and ability to route logs to your SIEM/S3.
- Whether trace IDs need to be preserved or pseudonymized for correlation.

2) What Redwood can do (summary)
- Configurable redaction: field-level and full-pattern masking (regex + ML-based PII detectors).
- Header controls: you can opt-out of persisting specific headers (e.g., Authorization, Cookie).
- Trace IDs: support for pseudonymization (SHA256 hashing with optional per-customer salt) or full redaction.
- Retention: per-customer configurable retention windows (0 days up to multi-year), default hosted retention is 30 days.
- Delivery: push logs to customer-owned S3, Splunk/Datadog via forwarders, or keep in Redwood encrypted store.
- Private options: Dedicated/Private deployments give you customer-managed KMS and VPC endpoints so logs never leave your network.

3) Questions for you (so we can scope design/POC)
- Do you require raw request/response bodies in logs for debug, or will pseudonymized/sanitized logs suffice?
- Which headers must be excluded (list)? Authorization, Set-Cookie, any custom auth headers?
- Retention window target (e.g., 90 days)? Is 90 days a hard requirement?
- Do you need trace IDs preserved exactly for cross-service correlation, or is a stable pseudonym acceptable?
- Any compliance mandates (PCI, GLBA, PSD2) that impose additional controls?

Attachments: attaching our SOC 2 summary and a short spreadsheet with logging questions filled in - please review and mark any firm requirements.

Next steps
- If you can reply with the answers above, Dylan and I will draft a short mutual action plan and sample redaction config for your security team.
- Proposed follow-up call: Tue Jul 6, 10:00 AM PT to review redaction config and SIEM integration.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Hi Marissa,

Appreciate the clear summary. A few quick answers from our side to help you scope:

- Raw bodies: We generally do not want full raw request/response bodies persisted if they contain PII. A sanitized/pseudonymized log will be acceptable for most cases. For a subset of error/forensic cases we may request temporary access to retained raw payloads (with strict audit).
- Headers: Please exclude Authorization and any cookie/auth headers. We also prefer masking of X-Auth-Token and X-Forwarded-For fields.
- Trace IDs: We need stable correlation across our services; a deterministic pseudonym (hash) is acceptable as long as it's consistent for a given trace id and reversible only by us.
- Retention: Our baseline requirement is 90 days for request/response logs.
- Compliance: We're PCI scoped for parts of our product and have internal requirements around cardholder data - would need confirmation that Redwood's redaction can be tuned to remove card numbers and related tokens.

I've looped in Rajiv (security) on this thread. Please also share the sample redaction config and an example of sanitized logs (remove any real customer data).

We can make Tue Jul 6 at 10:00 AM PT work - Rajiv will confirm.

Thanks,
Aisha Gupta
Head of Platform Security | FintechCo
aisha.gupta@fintechco.com

Subject: Re: Logging & redaction controls - post-demo follow-up

Great - thanks Aisha. Quick replies inline and next deliverables from our side:

- Raw bodies: we can support a workflow where sanitized logs are the default and raw payloads are retained in a restricted vault with time-limited access (audit entries + customer-managed KMS). We can scope the access workflow for forensic use.
- Headers: will exclude Authorization, Cookie; can add custom header list (please send exact header names).
- Trace IDs: we support deterministic pseudonymization (SHA256 with per-customer salt stored in your KMS for Dedicated/Private). Note that hashing is one-way; to make it reversible only by you we can support encrypting the trace id under your KMS.
- Retention: hosted default is 30 days but we can set 90 days for FintechCo on hosted Dedicated; Private deployment gives you full control.
- PCI: our redaction engine supports card number detection (Luhn + pattern rules) and will redact PANs before persistence. For extra compliance we can route logs to your S3/Splunk sink where you apply additional controls.

Deliverables from Redwood (by end of day Fri):
- Example sanitized log bundle (JSON) with common error cases (no real customer data).
- Proposed redaction config (regex + PII rules) for your review - will put this in the attached spreadsheet.
- SOC2 summary (attached) and pointer to security docs.

Links/attachments:
- redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (attached)

Thanks,
Marissa
